meta.title: A330 Phase Flows
meta.sources: A330P FCOM R17 PRO-NOR / PRO-ABN / PRO-NOR-SUP-SEC; QRH R35 22.02A; FCTM R5 PR-NP-CL, PR-AEP; FOM 125.1 5.5.15, 5.7.4, 6.3, 6.4, 11.2; PRC 3/9/26 p7, p8
meta.builders: box(t,s,r,call,q) fmc(t,s,r,q) sub(t,c) trig(t,r) cl(t,w,bold,cc) book(t,s) note(t) S(h,c,items,cite,appr); q = quote + [ref]
meta.roles: C=CM1 (CA seat) F=CM2 (FO seat) PF PM B=both; appr: all | ILS | ILScat (CAT II/III) | RNP | NPA
meta.normal_source: data/flows.json (quickref order and role) cross-checked to FCOM PRO-NOR idents; quotes are literal extract text

items.t: General
items.s: Obstructions near the aircraft · Engineering activity · Refueling activity
items.quote: When the flight crew arrives at the aircraft, they must check for, or be informed of any obstructions near the aircraft, engineering activity, or refueling activity, etc.

items.t: Wheel chocks
items.s: WHEEL CHOCKS ... CHECK
items.quote: If the wheel chocks are not in position, the flight crew must check that the parking brake is set with sufficient accumulator pressure.

items.t: Landing gear doors
items.s: LANDING GEAR DOORS ... CHECK POSITION
items.quote: If any landing gear door is open, do not pressurize the hydraulic systems until clearance is obtained from ground personnel.

items.t: APU area
items.s: APU AREA ... CHECK
items.quote: Observe that the APU inlet and outlet are clear.

items.t: Items marked * are the only steps after a transit stop without flight crew change.
ENG masters OFF · ENG START NORM
items.s: ENG 1, 2 MASTERS LEVERS ... OFF · ENG START selector ... NORM
items.quote: ENG 1, 2 MASTERS LEVERS ... OFF CM2 ENG START selector ... NORM CM2

items.t: Weather radar OFF *
items.s: WXR/PWS sw ... OFF · CAPT and F/O DISPLAY mode selectors ... OFF · GAIN ... AUTO · TURB ... AUTO
items.quote: * WXR/PWS sw ... OFF CM2 * CAPT DISPLAY mode selector ... OFF CM2 * F/O DISPLAY mode selector ... OFF CM2 * GAIN knob ... AUTO CM2 * TURB sw ... AUTO CM2

items.t: L/G lever DOWN
items.s: L/G lever ... DOWN
items.quote: L/G lever ... DOWN CM2

items.t: Wipers OFF
items.s: Both WIPER selectors ... OFF
items.quote: Both WIPER selectors ... OFF CM2

items.t: Batteries check / ELEC
items.s: Not supplied 6 h or more: BAT 1, BAT 2, APU BAT ... CHECK OFF then VOLTAGE ... CHECK ABOVE 25.5 V · then BAT pb-sw ... AUTO
items.quote: Battery voltage above 25.5 V ensures a charge above 50 %. After the check, the selector should remain on the APU position to avoid discharge of BAT 1 or 2.

items.t: RMP 1 and 2 CHECK ON
items.s: Green NAV light ... CHECK OFF · COM FREQUENCIES ... TUNE
items.quote: Use VHF 1 for ATC (only VHF 1 is available in emergency electrical configuration), VHF 2 for ATIS and company frequencies. VHF 3 is normally devoted to ACARS.

items.t: APU FIRE pb-sw
items.s: APU FIRE pb-sw ... CHECK IN and GUARDED
items.quote: APU FIRE pb-sw ... CHECK IN and GUARDED CM2

items.t: APU start · bleed
items.s: APU MASTER SW pb-sw ... ON · APU START pb-sw ... ON · when AVAIL: APU BLEED pb-sw ... ON · X-BLEED ... AUTO · COCKPIT / CABIN TEMP ... AS RQRD
items.quote: Do not use APU BLEED, if the ground personnel confirms that a LP or HP ground air unit is connected to the aircraft.

items.t: ADIRS * ALL IR MODE selector NAV
items.s: Complete alignment: first flight of the day · crew change · departure between 2° N and 2° S · GPS not available and poor NAVAID coverage · GPS not available and flight time more than 3 h
items.quote: A complete IRS alignment must be performed in the following cases: - Before the first flight of the day, or - When there is a crew change, or - When the departure airport is located between latitudes 2 ° north and 2 ° south, or - When the GPS is not available and the NAVAID coverage is poor on the expected route, or - When the GPS is not available and the expected flight time is more than 3 h.

items.t: Cockpit lights * AS RQRD
items.s: Set INT LT, FLOOD LT, INTEG LT (glareshield and FCU)
items.quote: Set INT LT, FLOOD LT, INTEG LT (included glareshield and FCU).

items.t: ATIS * OBTAIN
items.s: ATIS ... OBTAIN
items.quote: * ATIS ... OBTAIN CM2-CM3

items.t: MCDU ON (pre-initialization)
items.s: Short press of BRT switches ON the MCDU
items.quote: Short press of the BRT button will switch ON the MCDU, if it is OFF. Use the brightness buttons (BRT and DIM) to adjust the brightness as required.

items.t: EFB start (Flysmart)
items.s: ALL EFB ... START · EFB/eQRH VERSION ... CHECK · * EFB STATUS page ... INSERT/CHECK
items.quote: On the EFB STATUS page, each flight crewmember inserts and checks: - ACFT TYPE and ACFT REG - FLT NBR and FROM/TO (in agreement with the FMS ACTIVE/INIT page).

items.t: RCL pb * PRESS 3 s
items.s: recalls warnings cleared or cancelled during the last flight
items.quote: This action recalls all the warnings that the flight crew cleared or cancelled during the last flight.

items.t: LOGBOOK and MEL/CDL items * CHECK
items.s: deferred items list · crosscheck with ECAM recall · MEL / CDL acceptability and influence on the flight plan
items.quote: Check and discuss the MEL items (including the associated operational procedures, if any) and the CDL items. This includes the acceptability of the MEL and CDL items and the influence on the flight plan

items.t: OEB * CHECK
items.s: all crewmembers review and discuss applicable OEBs
items.quote: All flight crewmembers review and discuss together all OEBs and associated procedures applicable to the aircraft.

items.t: AIRCRAFT ACCEPTANCE * PERFORM
items.s: may be performed later, must be complete by end of Cockpit Preparation
items.quote: The aircraft acceptance can be performed later, but must be completed at the end of the Cockpit Preparation.

items.t: Jeppesen charts * PREPARE
items.quote: * JEPPESEN CHARTS ... PREPARE ALL

items.t: ACARS * INITIALIZE
items.quote: * ACARS ... INITIALIZE PF

items.t: Preliminary takeoff perf data * OBTAIN
items.s: per technical condition, NOTAM, runway condition, configuration
items.quote: The flight crew computes the preliminary performance data in accordance with the technical condition of the aircraft and/or any other criteria that may affect the aircraft performance (e.g. NOTAM, runway condition, aircraft configuration).

items.t: OXY · HYD · ENG OIL *
items.s: DOOR SD: OXY ... CHECK PRESSURE · HYD SD: RESERVOIR FLUID LEVEL ... CHECK WITHIN NORMAL RANGE · ENG SD: ENG OIL QUANTITY ... CHECK
items.quote: Check that the oil quantity is above the minimum. Refer to LIM-ENG Oil.

items.t: FLAPS CHECK POSITION · SPEED BRAKE * CHECK RETRACTED and DISARMED
items.quote: If flight control surface positions do not agree with the control handle positions, check with the maintenance crew before applying hydraulic power.

items.t: ACCU PRESS * CHECK · PARK BRK * ON · BRAKES PRESS * CHECK
items.s: ACCU PRESS in the green band; blue electric pump to recharge if required
items.quote: The ACCU PRESS indication must be in the green band. If required use the electric pump on blue hydraulic system to recharge the brake accumulator.

items.t: Alternate braking check
items.s: CHOCKS ... CHECK IN PLACE
items.quote: The purpose of this check is to verify, before the first flight of the day, the efficiency of the alternate braking system (absence of “spongy pedals”).

items.t: EMER EQPT CHECK
items.s: Life vests · Crash axe · Smoke hoods / portable oxygen and full-face masks · Portable fire extinguisher lockwired, gauge green · Oxygen masks · Flashlights · Escape ropes · PED Fire Containment Bag · Fire gloves
items.quote: - Portable fire extinguisher is lockwired and the pressure gauge indicator is in the green area - Oxygen masks are stowed - Flashlights are stowed - Escape ropes are stowed - PED Fire Containment Bag is stowed - Fire gloves are stowed

items.t: RAIN RPLNT indicators CHECK PRESSURE and QUANTITY
items.quote: Never use rain repellent to wash the windshield and never use it on a dry windshield.

items.t: GEAR PINS * CHECK ONBOARD and STOWED
items.s: three gear pins
items.quote: Check that the three gear pins are onboard and stowed.

items.t: PM: exterior walkaround (PRO-NOR-SOP-05) · PF: cockpit preparation
Overhead panel scan
items.s: * ALL WHITE LIGHTS ... OFF
items.quote: As a general rule, during the scan sequence of the overhead panel: * ALL WHITE LIGHTS ... OFF PF

items.t: Front instrument panels
items.s: * ISIS ... CHECK (brightness, IAS, altimeter, attitude, no flags) · * NORTH REF ... CHECK (TRUE blue light off)
items.quote: - Adjust brightness. - Check IAS, altimeter readings, altimeter settings and attitude display. - Check no flags - Reset attitude, if necessary.

items.t: Center pedestal
items.s: RMP 1 and 2 ... CHECK ON · Green NAV light ... CHECK OFF · COM FREQUENCIES ... TUNE
items.quote: RMP 1 and 2 ... CHECK ON PF Green NAV light ... CHECK OFF PF COM FREQUENCIES ... TUNE PF

items.t: FMS preparation · INIT A
items.s: TO/FROM ... CHECK · ALTN ... ENTER · FLT NBR ... CHECK · COST INDEX ... CHECK · CRZ FL/TEMP ... CHECK · TROPO ... AS RQRD · WINDS ... CHECK
items.quote: Press the INIT button on the MCDU to display the INIT A page. Check the TO/FROM field [1R] to confirm the correct flight plan uplink occurred.

items.t: FMS PREPARATION * CROSSCHECK
items.s: departure route waypoints and constraints · flight plan vs computerized flight plan · initial cruise altitude · total track miles · fuel at destination · performance data · TRANS ALT · SEC F-PLN
items.quote: The PM should have the same mental image of the intended departure procedure, trajectory, and constraints as the PF. The PM should check with the PF if anything is not clear.

items.t: Glareshield · EFIS control panel
items.s: * BAROMETRIC REFERENCE ... SET/CROSSCHECK · * FD ... CHECK ON · * LS ... AS RQRD · * ND MODE and RANGE ... AS RQRD · * ADF/VOR sw ... AS RQRD
items.quote: The maximum difference is: ±20 ft between both PFDs ±60 ft between ISIS and PFDs, 75 ft between PFDs and airport elevation (Refer to PRO-SPO-50 RVSM for more information).

items.t: Lateral consoles · OXYGEN MASK TEST PERFORM
items.s: ECAM DOOR/OXY SD: REGUL LO PR indication ... CHECK NOT DISPLAYED
items.quote: To prevent hearing damage to the ground crew connected to the intercom system, inform them that a loud noise may be heard in the headset when performing the oxygen mask test.

items.t: PFD and ND * CHECK
items.s: EFIS DMC selector ... CHECK NORM · PFD/ND not transferred · IAS, FMA, initial target ALT, altimeter, VSI, heading, attitude · ND heading, initial waypoint, VOR/ADF
items.quote: - Check IAS, FMA, initial target ALT, altimeter readings, VSI, altimeter settings, heading and attitude display.

items.t: ECAM control panel
items.s: * PRESS pb ... PRESS (CAB PRESS SD shows LDG ELEV AUTO) · * STS pb ... PRESS (INOP SYS compatible with MEL)
items.quote: Check that the CAB PRESS SD page displays LDG ELEV AUTO to confirm correct position of the LDG ELEV knob.

items.t: IRS ALIGN * CHECK
items.s: POSITION MONITOR: IRS in NAV, each IRS within 5 NM of FMS position · ND ROSE-NAV or ARC consistent with airport, SID, NAVAIDs
items.quote: On the POSITION MONITOR page, check that the IRS are in NAV mode, and check that the distance between each IRS and the FMS position is lower than 5 NM.

items.t: RELEASE VERSION / FITNESS / FOB / PDSC ... SENT
items.s: via OPS CTRL MSG page in ACARS
items.quote: Electronically accept latest flight release version fitness for duty, Fuel on Board and PDSC time via OPS CTRL MSG page in ACARS.

items.t: FUEL ON BOARD * CHECK
items.s: ECAM FOB = block fuel of the computerized flight plan · FUEL SD: balanced, CG within limits
items.quote: - Check that ECAM FOB corresponds to the block fuel of the computerized flight plan - On FUEL SD page, check that the fuel is correctly balanced and CG is within operational limits.

items.t: ATC clearance CONFIRM
items.s: VHF, ACARS (PDC) or CPDLC (DCL)
items.quote: Obtain ATC clearance via VHF, ACARS (PDC) or via CPDLC (DCL), Refer to PRO-SUP-46 Departure Clearance via CPDLC.

items.t: DEPARTURE LEGS VERIFICATION PERFORM
items.s: FMS waypoints vs Dispatch Release, Jeppesen Charts, ATC clearance
items.quote: The Departure Legs Verification is designed to verify the FMS waypoints against the Dispatch Release, the Jeppesen Charts, and ATC Clearance (if available).

items.t: DEPARTURE BRIEFING * PERFORM
items.s: Threat Based Departure Briefing (FOM Threat Based Departure Briefing/TPC)
items.quote: Perform a Threat Based Departure Briefing. For more information, refer to FOM "Threat Based Departure Briefing/ TPC".

items.t: Cockpit Preparation
PF sets
items.s: Strobes AUTO · Nav 1 · All others OFF

items.t: Lights table per the A330 quick reference (technique); switch states are the FCOM SOP lines quoted in each phase.
ACARS PERF page ... SELECT “*LOAD FMC”
items.s: FMS uploads the ACARS final weight data and takeoff performance
items.quote: The PF selects the “*LOAD FMC” prompt when it appears. This will allow the FMS to upload the ACARS final weight data and takeoff performance.

items.t: LOAD CLOSEOUT (LCO) CHECK
items.s: Flight number / date · Aircraft · Crew Count · TOF · TOW vs planned (MIN RLS FUEL adjustment?) · TOB · Jumpseat · ZFW/ZFWCG · NOTOC · AVI · FAM
items.quote: Both crew members carefully check the Load Closeout data is correct: - Flight number / date - Aircraft - Crew Count - Takeoff Fuel (“TOF”)

items.t: ZFW/ZFWCG CHECK/REVISE (PF, then PM)
items.s: green dot, F, S, VLS are computed from the entered ZFW and ZFWCG
items.quote: The characteristic speeds displayed on the MCDU (green dot, F, S, VLS) are computed from the ZFW and ZFWCG entered by the crew on the MCDU. Therefore, this data must be carefully checked before departure.

items.t: MIN RLS FUEL CHECK
items.s: ECAM FOB above Minimum Release Fuel
items.quote: Check that ECAM FOB is above Minimum Release Fuel on the flight plan.

items.t: TAKEOFF PERFORMANCE ... UPLINK FLX or UPLINK TOGA
items.s: FLAPS/THS reminder ... INSERT · manual entry: T.O SHIFT, V1 VR V2, FLX TO TEMP, THR RED/ACC, ENG OUT ACC
items.quote: The PF uplinks the Takeoff Data into the FMS PERF TO page. The crew can select to uplink either FLX or TOGA takeoff data.

items.t: FINAL TAKEOFF DATA (TPR/TLR) CHECK
items.quote: If the aircraft takes off from an intersection, insert a T.O shift value (even when GPS PRIMARY is active) to increase flight crew awareness of the runway length reduction.

items.t: MCDU pages
items.s: PF: FMS PERF TO page ... SELECT · PM: FMS F-PLN page ... SELECT
items.quote: It is recommended to display the PERF TAKEOFF page on the PF side.

items.t: SEATS, SEAT BELTS, HARNESSES, RUDDER PEDALS, ARMRESTS ... ADJUST
items.s: eyes aligned with the red and white balls
items.quote: The seat is correctly adjusted when the flight crew’s eyes are aligned with the red and white balls.

items.t: PUSHBACK/START CLEARANCE OBTAIN
items.s: ATC pushback/start clearance and ground crew clearance
items.quote: Obtain ATC pushback/start clearance and ground crew clearance.

items.t: Push / start clearance received
BEACON sw ON
items.quote: When cleared for start or pushback, set the BEACON sw to ON.

items.t: ATC ... SET FOR OPERATION
items.quote: ATC is set in accordance with airport requirements.

items.t: WINDOWS and DOORS CHECK CLOSED
items.s: sliding window handle fully forward, red indicator not visible · ECAM: all doors closed · cockpit door closed and locked
items.quote: - Check, on the ECAM lower display, that all the aircraft doors are closed - When required by FOM policies, check that the cockpit door is closed and locked (no cockpit door open/fault indication).

items.t: SLIDES CHECK ARMED
items.s: ECAM lower display
items.quote: Check, on the ECAM lower display, that all slides are armed.

items.t: THRUST LEVERS IDLE
items.quote: The engines start regardless of the thrust lever position. If the thrust levers are not set to IDLE, then thrust rapidly increases to the corresponding thrust lever position, causing a hazardous situation.

items.t: PARK BRK handle ON (if pushback not required)
items.s: BRAKES PRESS indicator ... CHECK
items.quote: When one brake temperature is above 300 °C , avoid applying the parking brake, unless operationally necessary.

items.t: Before Start
CA becomes PF if both pilots not trained (quickref).
PF sets ENG START selector to NORM
ENG START selector NORM
items.s: warm-up: idle at least 5 min cold (3 min warm) before high power
items.quote: After start, to avoid thermal shock, the engine must be operated at idle, or near idle for at least 5 min when engines are cold (3 min when engines are warm after a stop of 1.5 h or less) before advancing the thrust lever to high power.

items.t: GND SPLRS ARM
items.quote: GND SPLRS ... ARM PM

items.t: APU BLEED pb-sw OFF
items.s: avoids ingestion of engine exhaust gases
items.quote: This action enables to avoid ingestion of engine exhaust gases.

items.t: RUD TRIM RESET pb PRESS · RUD TRIM CHECK NEUTRAL
items.s: up to 0.6° residual is normal
items.quote: After the reset, the flight crew may observe an indication of up to 0.6 ° (L or R) in the RUD TRIM position indication.

items.t: ENG 1 and 2 ANTI-ICE pb-sw AS RQRD
items.s: ON for all ground operations in icing conditions
items.quote: Engine anti-ice must be set to ON during all ground operations, when icing conditions exist or are anticipated.

items.t: FLAPS lever SET FOR TAKEOFF · FLAPS CHECK POSITION
items.s: icing with rain, slush or snow: keep flaps retracted until the holding point
items.quote: Maintain the flaps retracted until the aircraft reaches the holding point of the takeoff runway. This action prevents contamination of the slats/flaps mechanism.

items.t: APU MASTER SW pb-sw OFF (if not required)
items.quote: If the APU is not required: APU MASTER SW pb-sw ... OFF PF

items.t: PITCH TRIM wheel CHECK
items.s: takeoff CG vs ECAM CG indication
items.quote: Check the takeoff CG on the PITCH TRIM wheel using the CG indication on the ECAM.

items.t: ECAM STATUS CHECK
items.s: PM checks, PF crosschecks: no STS reminder
items.quote: The PM checks and the PF crosschecks that there is no status reminder (STS) on the E/WD

items.t: N/WS DISC MEMO CHECK NOT DISPLAYED
items.quote: N/WS DISC MEMO ... CHECK NOT DISPLAYED PF

items.t: THRUST SETTING CROSSCHECK
items.s: E/WD FLEX temperature vs FMS PERF page
items.quote: The PF crosschecks the thrust setting (e.g. FLEX temperature) displayed on the E/WD with the FMS PERF page.

items.t: NWS TOWING FAULT LIGHT CHECK OFF
items.quote: NWS TOWING FAULT LIGHT ... CHECK OFF PF

items.t: After Start
PF: “CLEAR LEFT (RIGHT)” · PM: “CLEAR RIGHT (LEFT)”
items.s: when taxi clearance obtained
items.quote: When taxi clearance obtained CLEAR LEFT (RIGHT) CLEAR RIGHT (LEFT)

items.t: PF: “BRAKE CHECK”
items.s: BRAKE PEDALS ... PRESS · BRAKES ... CHECK · PM: BRAKE FAN AS RQRD · BRAKES PRESSURE ... CHECK AT ZERO
items.quote: If the aircraft was parked in wet conditions for a long time, the first brake application at low speed is less effective.

items.t: PF: “FLIGHT CONTROL CHECK”
items.s: PM: “FULL UP, FULL DOWN, NEUTRAL” · “FULL LEFT, FULL RIGHT, NEUTRAL” · PF: “RUDDER” PM: “FULL LEFT, FULL RIGHT, NEUTRAL” (PM follows pedals with feet)
items.quote: Check the flight controls at a convenient stage, before or during taxi.

items.t: ATC clearance CONFIRM
items.s: review before checking the AFS/Flight Instruments
items.quote: Review the ATC clearance before checking the AFS/Flight Instruments

items.t: AFS / flight instruments
items.s: CLEARED ALTITUDE ON FCU ... CHECK · HDG ON FCU ... IF REQUIRED, PRESET · BOTH FD ... CHECK ON · PFD/ND ... CHECK (both)
items.quote: If a heading is required by ATC after takeoff, in the case of a radar vector departure, preset the heading on the FCU. NAV mode will be disarmed.

items.t: AFS / flight instruments checked
TERR ON ND AS RQRD
items.s: radar on the PF side, TERR ON ND on the PM side
items.quote: Consider selecting the radar display on the PF side, and TERR ON ND on the PM side only.

items.t: AUTO BRK MAX pb-sw ON
items.quote: AUTO BRK MAX pb-sw ... ON PM

items.t: ATC CODE/MODE CONFIRM/SET FOR TAKEOFF
items.quote: ATC CODE/MODE ... CONFIRM/SET FOR TAKEOFF PM

items.t: ENG START selector AS RQRD
items.s: IGN/START: heavy rain, moderate or severe turbulence expected after takeoff
items.quote: Select IGN/START if: - Heavy rain, or - Moderate turbulence, or - Severe turbulence is expected after takeoff.

items.t: WXR/PWS sw SYS 1(2) · CAPT and F/O DISPLAY ALL
items.s: 30 s to fill the radar 3D buffer
items.quote: 30 s are necessary for the 3D buffer of the radar to be filled.

items.t: T.O CONFIG pb TEST
items.s: EWD displays T.O CONFIG NORMAL memo
items.quote: Press the T.O CONFIG on the ECP, and check that the EWD displays the T.O CONFIG NORMAL memo.

items.t: T.O MEMO CHECK NO BLUE
items.quote: Check that the EWD does not display any blue line in the T.O memo section.

items.t: Cabin NA/ADVISED · PM PA: “[FLIGHT ATTENDANTS SHOULD NOW] BE SEATED FOR TAKEOFF”
items.s: no less than two minutes prior to takeoff
items.quote: On Pax aircraft, The PM will make the Takeoff PA no less than two minutes prior to takeoff stating "[FLIGHT ATTENDANTS SHOULD NOW] BE SEATED FOR TAKEOFF".

items.t: Taxi
items.w: T.O CONFIG pb pressed and Takeoff Advisory PA complete

items.t: PF (or PM at PF request)
items.s: Taxi: Nose TAXI · Rwy Turnoff ON · Crossing a runway: Strobes ON · Land ON

items.t: Crossing a runway
items.s: STROBE sw ... ON · LAND LIGHT sw ... ON
items.quote: When crossing a runway: STROBE sw ... ON PF LAND LIGHT sw ... ON PF

items.t: Line-up clearance received
TAKEOFF RUNWAY CONFIRM
items.s: runway markings · runway lights · ILS signal (LOC centered after line up) · runway symbol on the ND · RAAS
items.quote: Confirm that the line up is performed on the intended runway and from the intended intersection.

items.t: TCAS Mode selector TA or TA/RA
items.s: TA/RA is the default; TA ONLY only at airports/procedures identified by Jeppesen 10-7 pages
items.quote: The flight crew should use the TA/RA mode as the default mode of the TCAS.

items.t: APPROACH PATH CLEAR OF TRAFFIC
items.s: visually and on the TCAS display
items.quote: Check that the approach path is clear of traffic, visually and using TCAS display on ND.

items.t: STROBE sw ON
items.s: PF may request the PM to set the exterior lights
items.quote: Set the STROBE sw to ON to cross or enter a runway. The PF can request the PM to set the exterior lights.

items.t: PACK 1 and PACK 2 pb-sw AS RQRD
items.s: packs OFF at least 20 s before takeoff thrust · APU bleed not permitted with wing anti-ice · APU bleed ON at least 20 s before takeoff thrust
items.quote: If a takeoff is performed with the packs OFF : The packs must be set to OFF at least 20 s before applying takeoff thrust.

items.t: Line-Up
Resume normal tasksharing if both pilots not trained (quickref).
TAKEOFF CLEARANCE OBTAIN
items.quote: TAKEOFF CLEARANCE ... OBTAIN PM

items.t: NOSE sw T.O · LAND sw ON
items.quote: NOSE sw ... T.O PF LAND sw ... ON PF

items.t: PF: “TAKEOFF” · THRUST 1.1 EPR
items.s: crosswind at or below 20 kt, no tailwind: SIDESTICK HALF FORWARD · tailwind or crosswind above 20 kt: SIDESTICK FULL FORWARD · BRAKES RELEASE · THRUST LEVERS FLX or TOGA
items.quote: Once the thrust levers are set to FLX or TOGA detent, the Captain maintains the hand on the thrust levers, until the aircraft reaches V1.

items.t: CHRONO START · PFD/ND MONITOR
items.s: PF: DIRECTIONAL CONTROL ... USE RUDDER
items.quote: If GPS PRIMARY LOST, check on the ND the FMS position: i.e. that the aircraft is on the runway centerline.

items.t: Below 80 kt · PM: “THRUST SET”
items.s: TAKEOFF THRUST ... CHECK (N1/EPR at rating limit, EGT) · PFD and ENG indications ... MONITOR
items.quote: Check that the actual N1/EPR of the individual engines has reached the N1/EPR rating limit, before the aircraft reaches 80 kt. Check EGT.

items.t: At 80 kt · SIDESTICK RELEASE
items.s: neutral at 100 kt
items.quote: Release the sidestick gradually to reach neutral at 100 kt.

items.t: At 100 kt · PM: “ONE HUNDRED KNOTS” · PF: “CHECKED”
items.s: below 100 kt the Captain may abort depending on circumstances · above 100 kt rejecting is a more serious matter
items.quote: • Below 100 kt, the Captain may decide to abort the takeoff, depending on the circumstances • Above 100 kt, rejecting the takeoff is a more serious matter.

items.t: At V1 · PM: “V1” (monitor or announce)
items.s: monitor the synthetic voice; announce if not triggered
items.quote: Monitor that the “V1” synthetic voice is triggered when reaching V1. If not, announce “V1”.

items.t: At VR · PM: “ROTATE”
items.s: PF: continuous rotation about 3°/s toward 15° (12.5° one engine failed) · after lift-off follow SRS
items.quote: - At VR, initiate the rotation with a positive sidestick input to achieve a continuous rotation rate of about 3 °/s, towards a pitch attitude of 15 ° (12.5 °, if one engine is failed)

items.t: PM: “POSITIVE RATE” · PF: “GEAR UP” · PM: “GEAR UP”
items.s: L/G lever SELECT UP · AP AS RQRD (above 100 ft AGL) · AP must be engaged for RNP AR below 0.3 NM
items.quote: Announce “Positive Rate” when the radio height is increasing, and a positive rate of climb is indicated on the altimeter and/or the vertical speed indicator.

items.t: PF: “AP 1(2) ON” (if AP engaged by PM)
items.s: above 100 ft AGL AP 1 or AP 2 may be engaged
items.quote: Above 100 ft AGL, AP 1 or AP 2 may be engaged. The AP must be engaged for RNP AR < 0.3 NM.

items.t: At thrust reduction altitude · THRUST LEVERS CL
items.s: when LVR CLB flashes · PM: PACK 1 ON after CLB thrust, PACK 2 ON at least 10 s later
items.quote: Move the thrust levers to the CL detent, when the flashing LVR CLB prompt appears on the FMA. Autothrust is now active.

items.t: PF (or PM at PF request)
items.s: Line up and wait: Strobes ON · Cleared for takeoff: Nose T.O. · Land ON

items.t: Above acceleration altitude (or once in climb phase)
At F speed · PF: “FLAPS 1” · PM: FLAPS 1 SELECT
items.s: PM: “SPEED CHECKED, FLAPS ONE” after checking the blue number on the ECAM flaps indicator
items.quote: At F speed FLAPS 1 ... ORDER PF FLAPS 1 ... SELECT PM

items.t: At S speed · PF: “FLAPS 0” · PM: FLAPS 0 SELECT
items.quote: At S speed FLAPS 0 ... ORDER PF FLAPS 0 ... SELECT PM

items.t: GND SPLRS DISARM · L/G CHECK UP · NOSE sw OFF · RWY TURN OFF sw OFF
items.quote: GND SPLRS ... DISARM PM L/G ... CHECK UP PM NOSE sw ... OFF PM RWY TURN OFF sw ... OFF PM

items.t: APU BLEED OFF · APU MASTER SW OFF (if APU supplied air for takeoff)
items.quote: If the APU was used to supply the air conditioning during takeoff: APU BLEED pb-sw ... OFF PM APU MASTER SW pb-sw ... OFF PM

items.t: ENG START selector AS RQRD
items.s: IGN/START in severe turbulence or heavy rain
items.quote: Select IGN/START, if severe turbulence or heavy rain is encountered.

items.t: TCAS mode selector TA/RA (if takeoff was TA only)
items.quote: If the takeoff was performed with TA only: TCAS mode selector ... TA/RA PM

items.t: ENG 1 and 2 ANTI ICE AS RQRD · WING ANTI ICE AS RQRD
items.s: engine anti-ice ON in icing conditions except climb/cruise with SAT below -40 °C
items.quote: Engine anti-ice must be set to ON when icing conditions exist or are anticipated, except during climb and cruise when the SAT is below -40 °C (-40 °F).

items.t: PF MCDU PERF CLB · PM MCDU F-PLN
items.s: PROG page shows OPT FL and MAX REC FL (0.3 g buffet margin)
items.quote: PM MCDU should be showing the F-PLN page (allowing PM to enter any ATC long-term revisions to the lateral or vertical flight plan).

items.t: CRZ FL SET AS RQRD
items.s: if ATC limits cruise below INIT A CRZ FL, insert the lower CRZ FL on PROG page or there is no CRZ phase transition
items.quote: If the ATC limits the CRZ FL to a lower level than the one entered in the INIT A page (or present on the PROG page), the flight crew must insert this lower CRZ FL in the PROG page.

items.t: Within 1 000 ft of clearance altitude · PF: “[leaving] for [cleared]” · PM: “CHECKED”
items.quote: When approaching within 1 000 ft of the clearance altitude, the PF will state, for example, "23 for 24" and the PM will calls out "CHECKED".

items.t: At transition altitude · PF: “SET STANDARD” · PM: “STANDARD CROSS-CHECKED, PASSING FL __ NOW” · PF: “CHECKED”
items.s: BAROMETRIC REFERENCE ... SET STD/CROSSCHECK
items.quote: - At the transition altitude, the barometric setting flashes on the PFD. The flight crew should set STD on the EFIS CP and on the standby altimeter.

items.t: Climbing 10 000 ft MSL
EFIS option: PF CSTR · PM ARPT
items.quote: EFIS Option: The PF will select CSTR The PM will select ARPT

items.t: LAND sw OFF
items.quote: AT 10 000 FT MSL LAND sw ... OFF PM

items.t: NO SMOKING sw ON, wait 3 s, AUTO
items.s: informs additional occupants of leaving sterile
items.quote: Cycle the NO SMOKING sw ON, wait three seconds, then back to AUTO to inform any additional aircraft occupants of leaving sterile, if required.

items.t: ECAM MEMO REVIEW · NAVAIDS CLEAR · SEC F-PLN AS RQRD · OPT FL/REC MAX FL CHECK
items.s: clear manually tuned VORs from RAD NAV
items.quote: Clear manually tuned VORs from RAD NAV page.

items.t: STARLINK * AS RQRD
items.s: ON passing 10 000 ft AAL when departing a station that does not allow its use
items.quote: When departing a destination that does not allow its use, Starlink shall be selected 'ON', passing 10 000 ft AAL.

items.t: SEAT BELTS sw AS RQRD (after 18 000 ft)
items.s: first time OFF after takeoff: Seat Belt Advisory PA per FOM
items.quote: When the seat belt sign is turned off for the first time after takeoff, Flight crews are required to make a 'Seat Belt Advisory' PA in accordance with FOM policy.

items.t: In cruise, the tasksharing is left to the flight crew appreciation (FCOM).
ECAM MEMO REVIEW · SD PAGES REVIEW
items.s: ENG oil press/temp · BLEED · ELEC GEN loads · HYD quantity · COND duct temps · F/CTL surface positions · FUEL distribution, trim tank, CG · DOOR oxygen pressure
items.quote: Periodically review the system display pages and, in particular, monitor the following:

items.t: FLIGHT PROGRESS CHECK
items.s: manually entered waypoint: track/distance to next, wind · every waypoint or at least every 60 min: FUEL check (FOB vs prediction vs CFP · no leak · FOB + FU = departure FOB)
items.quote: WHEN OVERFLYING A WAYPOINT, OR AT LEAST EVERY 60 MIN Check FUEL: - Check FOB (ECAM) and fuel prediction (FMGEC), and compare with the computerized flight plan - Check that there is no fuel leak

items.t: Fuel leak suspicion
items.s: FOB + FUEL USED vs departure: abnormally negative = suspect a leak · abnormally positive = suspect overread · check before any FUEL IMBALANCE procedure
items.quote: This check must also be performed each time a FUEL IMBALANCE procedure is necessary. Perform the check before applying the FUEL IMBALANCE procedure. If a fuel leak is confirmed, apply the FUEL LEAK procedure.

items.t: STEP FLIGHT LEVEL AS APPROPRIATE
items.quote: STEP FLIGHT LEVEL ... AS APPROPRIATE PF-PM

items.t: NAVIGATION ACCURACY MONITOR (if GPS PRIMARY LOST)
items.s: FMS PROGRESS page vs flown airspace
items.quote: Check on FMS PROGRESS page that the required navigation accuracy is appropriate according to the flown airspace. For more information, Refer to PRO SPO 51 PBN.

items.t: RADAR ADJUST AS APPROPRIATE
items.quote: RADAR ... ADJUST AS APPROPRIATE PF

items.t: OXYGEN MASK CHECK (if used)
items.s: properly stowed
items.quote: Check that the oxygen mask has been properly stowed (Refer to DSC-35-10 Description).

items.t: Any FMA change · PF announces · PM: “CHECKED”
items.s: armed modes with colour (G/S blue, LOC blue), active modes without colour (NAV, ALT)
items.quote: The PM should check and respond, "CHECKED" to all FMA changes called out by the PF.

items.t: Flap selection · PF: “FLAPS ONE” · PM: “SPEED CHECKED, FLAPS ONE”
items.s: PM checks the blue number on the ECAM flaps indicator
items.quote: PM selects the FLAPS lever position and replies after checking the blue number on the ECAM flaps indicator to confirm the correct selection has been made.

items.t: Gear selection · PF: “GEAR UP (DOWN)” · PM: “GEAR UP (DOWN)”
items.s: PM checks the red lights on the LDG GEAR indicator
items.quote: The PM selects the L/G lever position and replies after checking the red lights on the LDG GEAR indicator to confirm gear operation.

items.t: Transfer of control · “YOU HAVE CONTROL” · “I HAVE CONTROL”
items.quote: To give control : The pilot calls out "YOU HAVE CONTROL". The other pilot accepts this transfer by calling out "I HAVE CONTROL", before assuming PF duties.

items.t: Parking brake moved · “PARKING BRAKE SET / RELEASED”
items.s: whichever pilot operates it verbalizes its movement
items.quote: The flight crew member operating the parking brake must always verbalize its movement so that all flight crew are aware of its status.

items.t: Checklist complete · “__ CHECKLIST COMPLETE”
items.s: interruption: “HOLD CHECKLIST AT ___” then “RESUME CHECKLIST AT ___”
items.quote: If a checklist needs to be interrupted, announce : “HOLD CHECKLIST AT ___” and “RESUME CHECKLIST AT ___” for the continuation. Upon completion of a checklist announce : “__CHECKLIST COMPLETE”.

items.t: WEATHER AND LANDING INFORMATION OBTAIN
items.s: destination and alternate weather, runway conditions · low OAT: altitude corrections · JEPPESEN CHARTS ... PREPARE (all)
items.quote: Check the weather reports and runway conditions at destination and alternate airports. Airfield data, if any, should include the runway to be used for arrival.

items.t: BAROMETRIC REFERENCE PRESET
items.s: preset the QNH on the ISIS
items.quote: Preset the QNH on the ISIS.

items.t: ECAM STATUS CHECK
items.s: landing capability degradation, anything affecting approach and landing
items.quote: - Check the ECAM status page before completing the approach checks. Take particular note of any degradation in landing capability, or any other aspect affecting the approach and landing.

items.t: LANDING PERFORMANCE CHECK
items.s: request via ACARS · system failure not on the release: Flysmart landing distance · conditions changed: PM (RE)COMPUTE, PF CROSSCHECK · REV MAX is standard
items.quote: Request Landing Performance data via ACARS. For any system failure not listed on the dispatch release which affects landing performance a landing distance calculation must be computed using Flysmart.

items.t: FMS · ARRIVAL page COMPLETE/CHECK · F-PLN A page CHECK
items.s: APPR, STAR, TRANS, APPR VIA · approach and missed approach vs charts (ND PLAN) · speed and altitude constraints · do not modify the final approach · identify FDP and MAP
items.quote: - In all cases, do not modify the final approach (FAF to runway or MAP), including altitude constraints

items.t: RADIO NAV page CHECK · SELECTED NAVAIDS CHECK/MODIFY
items.s: ILS frequency and course · VOR/DME near the field in PROG BRG/DIST for NAV accuracy
items.quote: - For an ILS approach, check the frequency and course

items.t: DES WIND · PERF CRUISE · PERF DES CHECK
items.s: descent winds from cruise FL · cabin descent rate · MANAGED MACH/SPD; 250 kt below 10 000 ft default
items.quote: A speed limit of 250 kt below 10 000 ft is the defaulted speed in the managed speed descent profile. The flight crew may delete or modify it if necessary on the VERT REV at DEST page.

items.t: PERF APPR page COMPLETE/CHECK · PERF GO AROUND CHECK/MODIFY
items.s: guidance mode FLS or FINAL APP · QNH, temperature, average wind (no gust) · minimum · landing CONF FULL or CONF 3 · transition altitude · THR RED ALT and ACC ALT
items.quote: Insert the average wind given by the ATC or ATIS. Do not insert the gust value. During approach, the Ground Speed Mini function (managed speed mode) takes into account the instantaneous gust.

items.t: FUEL PRED CHECK · PROG CONSIDER · SEC F-PLN AS RQRD
items.s: EFOB destination, alternate, extra · BRG/DIST reference for energy management · SEC F-PLN to an alternative runway or circling runway before T/D
items.quote: The SEC F-PLN should be set before the top of descent, either to an alternative runway for destination, or to the landing runway in case of circling. In all cases, the routing to the alternate should be available.

items.t: FMS PREPARATION CROSSCHECK
items.s: PM checks all data entered by the PF, same mental image of arrival and approach
items.quote: After the PF prepares the FMS, the PM checks all the data entered in the FMS. The PM should have the same mental image of the intended arrival and approach procedure, trajectory, and constraints than the PF.

items.t: LDG ELEV CHECK
items.s: LDG ELEV AUTO on the CRUISE page and its value
items.quote: Check that the LDG ELEV AUTO is displayed on the CRUISE page, and check the associated value.

items.t: AUTO BRK AS RQRD
items.s: MAX not recommended at landing · short or contaminated: MED · long runways: LO
items.quote: Use of MAX mode is not recommended at landing. On short or contaminated runways, use MED mode. On long runways, LO mode is recommended

items.t: ARRIVAL LEGS VERIFICATION
items.s: PF reads from the ND (PLAN, CSTR, F-PLN) · PM verifies against the Jeppesen charts · repeat if the routing changes
items.quote: The PF reads from the “glass” (ND), and the PM verifies against the “paper” (Jeppesen Charts).

items.t: APPROACH BRIEFING PERFORM
items.s: Threat Based Approach Briefing (FOM Threat Based Arrival Briefing/TPC)
items.quote: Perform a Threat Based Approach Briefing. For more information, refer to FOM "Threat Based Arrival Briefing/TPC".

items.t: ENG 1 and 2 ANTI ICE AS RQRD · WING ANTI ICE AS RQRD
items.s: engine anti-ice ON before and during descent even below -40 °C SAT · ANTI ICE ON reduces the idle descent path angle
items.quote: Engine anti-ice must be set to ON before and during descent, even if the SAT is below -40 °C (-40 °F).

items.t: DESCENT CLEARANCE OBTAIN · CLEARED ALTITUDE ON FCU SET
items.s: PM obtains · PF sets, respecting safe altitudes
items.quote: When the flight crew obtains the ATC clearance, they should set the cleared altitude (FL) on the FCU taking into account the safe altitudes.

items.t: DESCENT INITIATE
items.s: DES mode at the FMS T/D · early descent: DES mode (V/S about 1 000 ft/min) · delayed: reduce toward green dot with ATC permission
items.quote: The standard method to initiate the descent is to engage the DES mode at the Top of Descent (T/D) computed by the FMS.

items.t: PF MCDU PROG/PERF DES · PM MCDU F-PLN
items.s: monitor VERT DEV and the level-off symbol · FPA (°) = ΔFL / DIST (NM)
items.quote: - From time to time during stabilized descent, the flight crew may select FPA to check that the remaining distance to destination is approximately the altitude change required divided by the FPA in degrees.

items.t: RATE OF DESCENT ADJUST, AS RQRD
items.s: increase speed before speed brakes · in DES mode on or below path do not use speed brakes; use OP DES with speed brakes
items.quote: In the DES mode, if the aircraft is on, or below the flight path and the ATC requires a higher rate of descent, do not use the speed brakes because the rate of descent is imposed by the planned flight path.

items.t: TERR ON ND AS RQRD
items.s: mountainous areas · radar PF side, TERR PM side · not with NAV ACCURACY LOW
items.quote: - If NAV ACCURACY is LOW, do not use the TERR on ND.

items.t: SEAT BELTS sw ON
items.s: no later than 18 000 ft on descent (or T/D if cruising lower)
items.quote: No later than 18 000 ft on descent (or at top of descent if cruising at lower altitude), turn the Seatbelt Sign ON.

items.t: CABIN PA · PM: “[Flight Attendants], please prepare the cabin for arrival and be seated for landing.”
items.s: no later than approximately 18 000 ft MSL · near T/D on short segments · when Early Sit Procedures are used
items.quote: "[Flight Attendants], please prepare the cabin for arrival and be seated for landing."

items.t: At transition level · BAROMETRIC REFERENCE SET/CROSSCHECK
items.s: PF: “SET QNH” · PM: “QNH CROSS-CHECKED, PASSING __ FT NOW” · PF: “CHECKED” · also update the PERF APPR QNH
items.quote: The flight crew must take into account any QNH change on the EFIS control panels, standby altimeter and on the FMS PERF APPR page.

items.t: STARLINK * AS RQRD
items.s: OFF approaching 10 000 ft AAL when the destination does not allow its use
items.quote: When approaching a destination that does not allow its use, Starlink shall be selected 'OFF', approaching 10 000 ft AAL.

items.t: Descending 10 000 ft AAL
LAND sw ON · SEAT BELTS sw ON · NO SMOKING sw ON, wait 3 sec, AUTO
items.quote: AT 10 000 FT AAL LAND sw ... ON PM SEAT BELTS sw ... ON PM NO SMOKING sw ... ON, wait 3 sec, AUTO PM

items.t: EFIS option pb CSTR (both sides)
items.quote: Select CSTR on both sides.

items.t: LS pb AS RQRD
items.s: ILS, GLS · ILS G/S out, LOC only, LOC B/C · FLS · SLS · check deviation scales and IDENT on the PFD
items.quote: The flight crew checks that: - Deviation scales are displayed on the PFD - The IDENT is properly displayed on the PFD.

items.t: NAVAIDS AS RQRD/CHECK
items.s: tuned and identified
items.quote: Ensure that the appropriate navaids are tuned and identified.

items.t: ENG START selector AS RQRD
items.s: IGN: standing water on the runway, heavy rain or severe turbulence in the approach or go-around area
items.quote: Select IGN if the runway is covered with standing water, or if heavy rain or severe turbulence is expected during approach or go-around area.

items.t: NAVIGATION ACCURACY MONITOR (if GPS PRIMARY LOST)
items.quote: If GPS PRIMARY LOST: NAVIGATION ACCURACY ... MONITOR PF

items.t: Approach
items.w: below 10 000 ft AAL and baro ref set

items.t: At taxi speed CA becomes PF if both pilots not trained (quickref).
F-PLN SEQUENCING ADJUST
items.s: TO waypoint on the ND must remain meaningful · NAV sequences automatically · HDG/TRK only when close to the route
items.quote: - A good clue to monitor the proper F-PLN sequencing is the TO waypoint on the upper right side of the ND, which should remain meaningful

items.t: APPROACH PHASE CHECK/ACTIVATE · PF: “ACTIVATE APPROACH PHASE” · PM: “APPROACH PHASE ACTIVATED”
items.s: automatic at DECEL in NAV · in HDG/TRK activate about 15 NM from touchdown on PERF DES
items.quote: - If the aircraft is in HDG or TRK mode, approximately 15 NM from touchdown activate and confirm APPR phase on the PERF DES page.

items.t: MANAGED SPEED CHECK · FLIGHT PATH MONITOR
items.s: ATC speed: selected, then back to managed · NAV: V/DEV · HDG/TRK: energy circle on the ND
items.quote: - In HDG or TRK mode, use the energy circle on ND representing the required distance to land.

items.t: SPEED BRAKES lever AS RQRD
items.s: VLS increases with speed brakes; ensure speed margin before extension and before a turn (Alpha-Floor)
items.quote: • If the speed brakes are extended, the flight crew should ensure that appropriate speed margin exists before the beginning of a turn.

items.t: PM: “RADIO ALTIMETER ALIVE” · PF: “CHECKED”
items.s: keep RA in scan to landing
items.quote: Flight crew awareness, flight crew should now keep RA in scan to landing.

items.t: At green dot · PF: “FLAPS 1” · PM: FLAPS 1 SELECT
items.s: more than 3 NM before the FDP · established with FLAPS 1 and S speed at or above 2 500 ft AGL · TCAS TA or TA/RA
items.quote: - For decelerated approaches, the aircraft must reach or be established on the final descent with FLAPS 1 and S speed at or above 2 500 ft AGL

items.t: At 2 500 ft AGL minimum · PF: “FLAPS 2” · PM: FLAPS 2 SELECT
items.s: intercept below 2 500 ft AGL (2 000 minimum): FLAPS 2 at one dot below the path · high speed: extend the gear, speed brakes not recommended
items.quote: - For ILS, GLS , SLS , FLS , if the aircraft intercepts the flight path below 2 500 ft AGL (2 000 ft AGL minimum), select FLAPS 2 at one dot below the flight path

items.t: When flaps at 2 · PF: “GEAR DOWN” · PM: L/G lever SELECT DOWN
items.s: AUTO BRK CONFIRM · GROUND SPOILERS ARM · cleared for approach: NOSE TAXI, RWY TURN OFF ON · cleared to land: NOSE T.O
items.quote: If the runway conditions have changed from the arrival briefing, consider another braking mode.

items.t: When gear is down · PF: “FLAPS 3” · PM: FLAPS 3 SELECT
items.s: ECAM WHEEL SD CHECK: three green, at least one green triangle per strut, LDG GEAR DN memo
items.quote: - Check for three green indications on the landing gear indicator panel. At least one green triangle on each landing gear strut on the WHEEL SD page is sufficient to indicate that the landing gear is downlocked.

items.t: PF: “FLAPS FULL” · PM: FLAPS FULL SELECT
items.s: decelerates to VAPP · correct TO waypoint on the ND
items.quote: - Check that the aircraft decelerates to VAPP - Check correct TO waypoint on the ND.

items.t: A/THR CHECK IN SPEED MODE OR OFF · WING ANTI ICE OFF · SLIDING TABLE STOW · LDG MEMO CHECK NO BLUE
items.s: wing anti-ice ON only in severe icing
items.quote: Switch the WING ANTI ICE pb-sw ON, only in severe icing conditions.

items.t: Landing
FLIGHT PARAMETERS MONITOR
items.s: PM calls: speed below target -5 kt or above +10 kt · pitch below 0° or above +10° · bank more than 7° · descent rate more than 1 000 ft/min
items.quote: • The speed goes lower than the speed target -5 kt, or more than the speed target +10 kt • The pitch attitude goes lower than 0 °, or more than +10 ° nose up • The bank angle becomes more than 7 ° • The descent rate becomes more than 1 000 ft/min.

items.t: Selected speed if not managed: S after FLAPS 1, F after FLAPS 2, VAPP after LDG FLAPS. Extend flaps at VFE -15 kt when possible.
Stabilized approach
items.s: correct lateral and vertical path · landing configuration · thrust stabilized above idle at target speed · no excessive deviation
items.quote: If one of the above-mentioned conditions is not satisfied, the flight crew must initiate a go-around, unless they estimate that only small corrections are required to recover stabilized approach conditions.

items.t: FAF · PM: “(Fix), (PFD altitude), (altimeter setting), CHECKED” · PF: “CHECKED”
items.s: criteria not met: PM “UNSTABLE, GO AROUND” · PF “GO AROUND - FLAPS”
items.quote: FAF (Fix name)_____, (PFD altitude)_____, (altimeter setting)_____, CHECKED

items.t: 1 000 ft AFE (stabilized gate) · PF: “STABLE” · PM: “CHECKED”
items.s: out of limits: PF “CORRECTING SPEED / VERTICAL SPEED” · config not met: PF “UNSTABLE, GO AROUND - FLAPS” (PM calls it if PF does not)
items.quote: 1 000 ft AFE (Stabilized Gate)(6) If 1 000 ft configuration criteria are met: STABLE

items.t: 500 ft AFE (go-around gate) · PM: “STABLE” · PF: “CHECKED”
items.s: not met: PM “UNSTABLE, GO AROUND” · PF “GO AROUND - FLAPS”
items.quote: 500 ft AFE (Go-Around Gate)(6) If 500 ft criteria are met: STABLE

items.t: Deviation callouts (PM) · PF: “CORRECTING”
items.s: “SPEED” +10/-5 kt · “SINK RATE” more than 1 000 ft/min below 1 000 ft · “ALTITUDE” · “LOC” / “GLIDESLOPE” 1/2 dot · “COURSE” · “TRACK” 0.1 NM · “V DEV” 1/2 dot · “LAT DEV” · PAPI
items.quote: The PM calls out if excessive deviation occurs: - LOC: ½ dot - G/S: ½ dot.

items.t: APPR pb on FCU PRESS · PF: “ARM APPROACH”
items.s: when cleared, on the intercept trajectory, LOC deviation available · arms LOC and G/S · capture no sooner than 3 s after arming
items.quote: - Press the APPR pb when all of the following is applicable: • The aircraft is cleared for the approach • The aircraft is on the intercept trajectory for the final approach course • LOC deviation is available on the PFD.

items.t: BOTH APs ENGAGE
items.s: above 5 000 ft AGL FMA shows CAT 1 · below 5 000 ft AGL the actual capability
items.quote: - When APPR mode is selected, AP1 and AP2 should be engaged - Above 5 000 ft AGL, the FMA displays CAT 1 - Below 5 000 ft AGL, the FMA displays the correct approach capability for the intended approach.

items.t: LOC CHECK ARMED · G/S CHECK ARMED · LOC CAPTURE MONITOR · G/S CAPTURE MONITOR
items.s: PF announces FMA: “LOC blue”, “G/S blue”, “LOC*”, “G/S*”
items.quote: LOC ... CHECK ARMED PF G/S ... CHECK ARMED PF LOC CAPTURE ... MONITOR PF G/S CAPTURE ... MONITOR PF

items.t: GO-AROUND ALTITUDE SET · PF: “SET GA ALTITUDE __ FT” · PM: “GA ALTITUDE SET”
items.s: at G/S*, or PF sets: “GA ALTITUDE SET” · PM: “CHECKED”
items.quote: GO-AROUND ALTITUDE ... SET BOTH

items.t: Glide interception from above
items.s: established on the LOC · gear down, at least CONF 2 · APPR ARM/CHECK ARMED · LOC CHECK ENGAGED · FCU ALTITUDE SET ABOVE A/C ALTITUDE · V/S MODE SELECT (1 500 ft/min initially)
items.quote: Select V/S 1 500 ft/min initially. V/S in excess of 2 000 ft/min will result in the speed increasing towards VFE.

items.t: FLIGHT PARAMETERS MONITOR · PM: “LOC” / “GLIDESLOPE” at 1/2 dot
items.quote: The PM calls out if excessive deviation occurs: - LOC: ½ dot - G/S: ½ dot.

items.t: At 350 ft RA · LAND mode CHECK ENGAGED/ANNOUNCE
items.s: no LAND mode: autoland not authorized
items.quote: If no LAND mode, autoland is not authorized.

items.t: Entered minimum +100 ft · PM: “ONE HUNDRED ABOVE” · PF: “CHECKED”
items.quote: AT ENTERED MINIMUM +100 ft ONE HUNDRED ABOVE ... MONITOR OR ANNOUNCE PM

items.t: At minimum · PM: “MINIMUM” · PF: “CONTINUE” (AP AS RQRD) or “GO-AROUND”
items.s: below minimum visual references are the primary reference until landing
items.quote: Below minimum, the visual references must be the primary reference until landing.

items.t: APPROACH MINIMUM DETERMINE
items.s: lowest achievable minimum: crew qualification · Operating Manual · aircraft status · airport status · CAT III no DH: enter NO in the DH field
items.quote: - For CAT III with no DH, the flight crew should enter NO in the DH field of the MCDU to avoid false "HUNDRED ABOVE" or "MINIMUM" auto callouts which would not be applicable.

items.t: APPROACH BRIEFING PERFORM
items.s: task sharing and callouts · management of degraded guidance · low visibility procedures at the airport
items.quote: For CAT II, CAT III, approaches, review the following items on top of the usual briefing: - Task sharing and callouts - Management of degraded guidance - Low visibility procedures at the airport.

items.t: LAND on FMA (350 ft RA) · PF: “LAND” · PM: “CHECKED”
items.quote: LAND on FMA (350’ RA) "LAND" "CHECKED"

items.t: CAT II · DA(H) +100 ft · PM: “100 ABOVE” · PF: “CHECKED”
items.s: DA(H): PM “MINIMUM” · PF “CONTINUE” or “GO AROUND, FLAPS”
items.quote: DA(H) + 100’ “CHECKED” "100 ABOVE"(1) DA(H) “CONTINUE”, or "MINIMUM"(1) “GO AROUND, FLAPS”

items.t: CAT III · 200 ft RA (alert height) · PM: “ALERT” · PF: “CONTINUE” or “GO AROUND, FLAPS”
items.s: no failure at 200 ft
items.quote: At 200 ft (Alert Height) if no failure ALERT ... ANNOUNCE PM CONTINUE ... ANNOUNCE PF

items.t: 40 ft RA · PM: “FLARE” or “NO FLARE” · Rollout · PM: “ROLLOUT”
items.s: no FLARE on the FMA: go-around, or manual landing if visual references are sufficient
items.quote: If the FMA does not display FLARE, perform a go-around, or a manual landing if visual references are sufficient.

items.t: Degraded guidance above 1 000 ft AGL
items.s: ECAM/QRH PROCEDURE COMPLETE · APPROACH AND LANDING CAPABILITY CHECK · REQUIRED EQUIPMENT CHECK · RVR CHECK, DH ADJUST, briefing UPDATE · not complete at 1 000 ft: GO-AROUND
items.quote: If the flight crew does not complete all the above actions at 1 000 ft: GO-AROUND ... PERFORM PF

items.t: Degraded guidance below 1 000 ft AGL · GO-AROUND PERFORM
items.s: below 200 ft CAT3 DUAL: continue unless AUTOLAND warning · AUTOLAND warning: GO-AROUND
items.quote: Below 200 ft (Alert Height) for CAT3 DUAL : The automatic approach may be continued unless the AUTOLAND warning is triggered.

items.t: At 350 ft RA · LAND on FMA CHECK/ANNOUNCE · ILS COURSE on PFD CHECK
items.s: course pointer vs runway track more than 5°: go-around or manual landing
items.quote: If the ILS course pointer and the runway track differ by more than 5 °, perform a go-around, or a manual landing if visual references are sufficient.

items.t: At 40 ft RA · FLARE on FMA CHECK/ANNOUNCE · FLARE MONITOR
items.quote: AT 40 FT RA FLARE ON FMA ... CHECK/ANNOUNCE PM

items.t: At 30 ft RA · THR IDLE on FMA CHECK · THRUST IDLE CHECK
items.quote: AT 30 FT RA THR IDLE ON FMA ... CHECK PM THRUST IDLE ... CHECK PM

items.t: At 10 ft RA · automatic “RETARD” · ALL THRUST LEVERS IDLE
items.s: autothrust disconnects · monitor lateral guidance with external references
items.quote: Monitor the lateral guidance by using external references.

items.t: At touchdown · ROLL OUT on FMA CHECK/ANNOUNCE · reversers · GND SPLRS · DECEL
items.s: NWS or anti-skid failure: AP OFF at touchdown
items.quote: In the case of NWS or Anti-Skid failure, set the AP OFF at touchdown.

items.t: End of roll out · ALL REVERSER LEVERS STOW · AP OFF
items.s: before leaving the runway at the latest

items.quote: The PF orders the PM to set both FDs off.

items.quote: When the aircraft is below the FCU altitude, the flight crew must apply the GO AROUND procedure.

items.t: AP OFF (manual landing)
items.quote: FOR MANUAL LANDING AP ... OFF PF

items.t: Around 40 ft RA · FLARE PERFORM · ALL THRUST LEVERS IDLE
items.s: PM: ATTITUDE MONITOR · automatic “RETARD” at 20 ft is a reminder · ground spoilers inhibited with a lever above IDLE
items.quote: Move the thrust levers to the IDLE detent, and begin a gentle progressive flare to enable the aircraft to touch down without a prolonged float.

items.t: At touchdown · DEROTATION INITIATE · ALL REVERSER LEVERS REV MAX or REV IDLE
items.s: reverse immediately after main gear touchdown = full-stop landing · REV MAX: emergency, decel not as expected, failure, long flare, tailwind
items.quote: The flight crew must select reverse thrust immediately after main landing gear touchdown.

items.t: PM: “SPOILERS” (or “NO SPOILERS”)
items.s: no spoilers: thrust levers IDLE detent, both reversers MAX REV, brake pedals fully pressed
items.quote: - If no ground spoilers are extended: • Check that all thrust levers are set to IDLE detent • Set both thrust reverser levers to MAX REV, and fully press the brake pedals.

items.t: PM: “REVERSE GREEN” (or “NO REVERSE ENGINE _” / “NO REVERSE”)
items.quote: - If reverser(s) do not deploy as expected, one of the main deceleration means is lost. The flight crew should consider adapting the available deceleration means to stop the aircraft.

items.t: DIRECTIONAL CONTROL ENSURE
items.s: rudder pedals · no sidestick inputs · directional problem: REV IDLE · no tiller before taxi speed
items.quote: - During rollout, avoid sidestick inputs (either lateral or longitudinal)

items.t: AUTO BRK CHECK/ANNOUNCE · AUTOBRAKE MONITOR
items.s: BRK LO or BRK MED on the FMA · PM: “AUTOBRAKE OFF” if it disengages · PF: “MANUAL BRAKING”
items.quote: During all the rollout, the PM monitors that the FMA displays BRK LO or BRK MED and calls out if the autobrake mode disengages.

items.t: PM: “DECEL” (or “NO DECEL”)
items.s: felt, and confirmed by the speed trend on the PFD
items.quote: The flight crew feels the deceleration. The flight crew checks the speed trend on the PFD to confirm the deceleration.

items.t: At 70 kt · PM: “SEVENTY KNOTS” · PF: “CHECKED” · ALL REVERSER LEVERS IDLE
items.s: high reverse at low speed only in an emergency
items.quote: It is recommended to reduce reverse thrust when passing 70 kt . However high levels of reverse thrust may be used in order to control aircraft speed in case of an emergency.

items.t: At taxi speed · ALL REVERSER LEVERS STOW
items.s: before leaving the runway · no reverse on taxiways except emergency
items.quote: When the aircraft reaches the taxi speed, and before it leaves the runway, stow the reversers.

items.t: Before 20 kt · AUTO BRK DISENGAGE
items.s: use the brake pedals to disengage
items.quote: Disengage the autobrake to avoid some brake jerks at low speed. The flight crew should use brake pedals to disengage the autobrake.

items.s: avoids radiating persons at the gate
items.quote: Switching the radar and radar display to OFF after landing avoids risk of radiating persons at the gate area.

items.t: ENG START selector NORM
items.quote: ENG START selector ... NORM PM

items.t: FLAPS RETRACT
items.s: icing approach or slush/snow: do not retract until after shutdown and ground crew confirms clear · OAT above 40 °C: consider CONF 1 during transit
items.quote: - If the approach was performed in icing conditions, or if the runway was contaminated with slush or snow, do not retract the flaps until after engine shutdown, and after the ground crew confirmed that flaps and slats are clear of obstruction due to ice.

items.t: TCAS STBY
items.quote: TCAS ... STBY PM

items.t: APU AS RQRD
items.s: start fails: wait 3 min · three consecutive attempts: wait 60 min · may delay start until before shutdown, check AVAIL first
items.quote: If the start attempt fails, wait for 3 min, then set the APU START pb-sw to ON again. This ensures that the fuel feed line of the APU is sufficiently pressurized. After three consecutive start attempts, the flight crew must wait 60 min before they perform a new start attempt.

items.t: ENG ANTI ICE AS RQRD
items.s: ground idle is increased: control taxi speed
items.quote: If engine anti-ice is used, carefully control taxi speed, particularly on wet or slippery surfaces because ground idle is increased.

items.t: After Landing
ACCU PRESS indicator CHECK · PARK BRK handle ON
items.s: low accumulator pressure: chocks before shutdown · brake above 300 °C: release after chocks
items.quote: The ACCU PRESS indication must be in the green band. In case of low accumulator pressure, chocks are required before engine shutdown.

items.t: ANTI ICE OFF
items.quote: ANTI ICE ... OFF PM

items.t: APU BLEED pb-sw AS RQRD
items.s: ON and wait for the APU BLEED memo, then shut down the engines immediately
items.quote: - Shut down the engines immediately after the display of the APU BLEED memo to prevent engine exhaust fumes from entering the air conditioning.

items.t: All ENG MASTER levers OFF
items.s: no less than 1 min after high thrust · APU START CHECK AVAIL or EXT A(B) ON first
items.quote: No less than 1 min after high thrust operations: All ENG MASTER levers ... OFF PF

items.t: FUEL PUMPS OFF
items.quote: FUEL PUMPS ... OFF PM

items.t: WING sw OFF · BEACON sw OFF · other exterior lights AS RQRD (NAV & LOGO 1)

items.quote: Turn off the beacon lights when all engines spooled down.

items.t: ATC STBY

items.quote: SEAT BELTS sw ... OFF PF

items.quote: Check that the slides are disarmed on the DOOR/OXY SD page. Warn the cabin crew, if any slide is not disarmed.

items.t: FUEL QUANTITY CHECK
items.s: FOB + fuel used = departure FOB; unusual discrepancy = maintenance
items.quote: Check that the sum of the fuel on board and the fuel used is consistent with the fuel on board at departure. If the flight crew detects a discrepancy that is not usual, maintenance action is due.

items.t: GROUND CONTACT ESTABLISH · PARK BRK handle ON
items.s: “chocks in” hand signal · release after chocks if a brake is above 300 °C (150 °C with fans)
items.quote: The parking brake should be set. If one brake temperature is above 300 °C (or above 150 °C with brake fans ON), the parking brake should be released after chocks are in place.

items.quote: Complete the logbook according to the STATUS page.

items.quote: Dim EFIS, ECAM and MCDU display units.

items.t: PARK BRK handle CHECK ON
items.s: reduces accumulator leak rate
items.quote: Keep the parking brake on to reduce hydraulic leak rate in the brake accumulator.

items.t: OXYGEN CREW SUPPLY pb OFF
items.quote: OXYGEN CREW SUPPLY pb ... OFF

items.t: All IR MODE selectors OFF
items.s: wait at least 10 s before removing electrical supply · not above 82° N/S during transits
items.quote: After turning off the ADIRS, wait at least 10 s before turning off the electrical supply, in order to ensure that the ADIRS memorize the latest data.

items.t: EXTERIOR LIGHTS OFF · GND SELECT CTL sw AS RQRD · APU BLEED OFF · EXT PWR AS RQRD · APU MASTER SW OFF

items.quote: Turn off the APU after all passengers disembarked.

items.quote: EMER EXIT LT sw ... OFF CM2 SIGNS sw ... OFF CM2

items.s: wait for the APU flap to close (about 2 min after AVAIL out)
items.quote: Wait until the APU flap is fully closed (about 2 min after APU AVAIL light goes out) before switching off the APU battery. Switching the batteries off before the APU flap is closed may cause smoke in the cabin during the next flight.

items.t: WINDOWS CHECK CLOSED · EFB APPLICATIONS CLOSE
items.quote: WINDOWS ... CHECK CLOSED CM1-CM2

items.t: Securing the Aircraft
THRUST LEVERS TOGA
items.s: set TOGA detent even if TOGA thrust is not required, then retard as required (CL for A/THR) · not briefly TOGA: no GO AROUND phase, destination sequences within 7 NM
items.quote: If TOGA thrust is not required, set the thrust levers to TOGA detent then retard the thrust levers as required. This enables to engage the GO-AROUND phase, with associated AP/FD modes.

items.t: ROTATION PERFORM
items.s: toward 15° (about 12.5° one engine out) then follow SRS · near the ground avoid excessive rotation rate (tail strike)
items.quote: Initiate rotation towards 15 ° of pitch with all engines operative (approximately 12.5 ° if one engine is out) to get a positive rate of climb then follow SRS Flight Director pitch orders.

items.t: PF: “GO AROUND - FLAPS” · PM: FLAPS RETRACT ONE STEP · “FLAPS __”

items.s: PM: GND SPLRS DISARM · L/G CHECK UP · NOSE OFF · RWY TURN OFF OFF · other lights AS RQRD (LAND may stay ON)
items.quote: The flight crew can maintain the LAND sw set to ON, according to airline policy or regulatory recommendations.

items.quote: GO AROUND decision GO AROUND - FLAPS Flaps retraction FLAPS__ Gear retraction POSITIVE CLIMB GEAR UP GEAR UP

items.t: 1 · Complete the non-normal procedure (ECAM / QRH)
items.quote: Failure that requires landing (LAND ASAP, FIRE, Engine Failure).

items.t: 2 · Does the failure require diversion? YES: DIVERT (coordinate with SOCC)
items.s: failures requiring diversion: LAND ASAP, FIRE, engine failure · insufficient fuel after a component failure · one GEN remaining
items.quote: Failure that requires landing (LAND ASAP, FIRE, Engine Failure).

items.t: 3 · If not required: are the risks of continuing higher than the risks of diverting?
items.s: continue to destination, or DIVERT (coordinate with SOCC)
items.quote: Please reference FCOM-PRO-SPO-40: EXTENDED RANGE OPERATIONS

items.t: No impact on ETOPS operations for amber or green ECAM messages / memos or any single failure other than an engine failure (PRC p8).
One engine inoperative · land at the NEAREST SUITABLE airport
items.s: 14 CFR 121.565 · Captain judgment after considering all relevant factors · assign PF/PM per TEM
items.quote: 14 CFR 121.565 requires the Captain of a two-engine aircraft with one engine inoperative to land at the nearest suitable airport where, in the Captain’s judgment after considering all relevant factors, a safe landing can be made.

items.t: Flight crews will
items.s: maintain awareness of suitable airports · current diversion plan in mind · weather and NOTAMs at the diversion airport · coordinate with Dispatch · include the diversion plan in the brief after a rest period
items.quote: Flight Crews will: • Maintain awareness of suitable airports • Have a current diversion plan in mind • Keep track of weather and NOTAMs at diversion airport • Be prepared to coordinate with Dispatch in the event of an actual diversion

items.t: 180 turn near a fuel-critical ETP
items.s: turn time is not in the flight planning fuel or time
items.quote: If a 180 turn is necessary near a fuel-critical ETP, the Flight Crew should be aware that the time to complete the turn is not factored in the fuel or time calculations by the flight planning system.

items.t: Nearest suitable: factors
items.s: configuration, weight, systems, fuel · enroute wind and weather at diversion altitude · minimum altitudes · fuel burn · terrain, weather, wind · runways and surface · navaids and lighting · RFFS · disembarkation facilities · PIC familiarity · geo-political
items.quote: • Approach navigation aids and lighting available • Rescue and fire fighting services (RFFS) at the diversion airport • Facilities for passenger and crewmember disembarkation and accommodations • PIC’s familiarity with the airport

items.t: Never sufficient to fly beyond the nearest suitable (one engine inop)
items.s: fuel to fly beyond · passenger accommodation other than safety · maintenance or repair resources
items.quote: When operating a two-engine aircraft with one engine inoperative, none of the following factors should be considered sufficient justification to fly beyond the nearest suitable airport: • The fuel supply is sufficient to fly beyond the nearest suitable airport • Passenger accommodation other than passenger safety • Availability of maintenance and/or repair resources

items.t: Decision to continue after a system failure
items.s: coordinate with Dispatch: re-evaluate capabilities, new Flight Plan/Release before the EEP if required
items.quote: If an updated Flight Plan/Dispatch Release is required and the flight has not passed the EEP, then the new Flight Plan/Dispatch Release must be received prior to the EEP.

items.t: ATC · advise as soon as practicable, remind of the aircraft type, request expeditious handling
items.quote: If contingency procedures are employed as a result of an engine shutdown or system failure, the Captain should advise ATC as soon as practicable of the situation, reminding ATC of the type of aircraft involved, and make a request for expeditious handling.

items.t: Simultaneously: SET MCT and DISCONNECT AUTOTHRUST
items.s: instinctive disconnect pb · do not delay the descent · do not decelerate below green dot
items.quote: At high flight levels, close to the weight limits, the aircraft speed quickly reduces. Thus, the flight crew should not delay descent. The crew must not decelerate below green dot.
items.ref: PRC p7 Engine Failure During Cruise

items.t: PULL SPEED - GREEN DOT
items.s: initially green dot to minimize the rate of descent
items.quote: PULL SPEED - GREEN DOT
items.ref: PRC p7 Engine Failure During Cruise

items.t: Oceanic: ESTABLISH 5 NM OFFSET
items.s: turn at least 30° L/R to a parallel same-direction track offset 5 NM · pull heading and/or 5 NM offset on the F-PLN · below FL290 (or when cleared) maneuver as required
items.quote: Leave the cleared route/track by turning at least 30º to the L/R to establish a parallel same direction track offset by 5NM. Pull heading and/or insert a 5NM L/R offset on MCDU FPLN page.
items.ref: PRC p7 Engine Failure During Cruise

items.t: PULL FL 200 · START APU
items.s: FL200 until the final drift down altitude is determined
items.quote: Initially set FL200 until the final Drift Down Altitude is determined.
items.ref: PRC p7 Engine Failure During Cruise

items.t: Exterior lights ON · monitor TCAS · declare MAYDAY on VHF or 121.5 · CPDLC EMERG ADS-C ON
items.s: non-radar: keep transmitting position and intentions until clear of traffic
items.quote: Declare an Emergency (MAYDAY): Transmit position and intentions on current VHF ATC frequency or 121.5.
items.ref: PRC p7 Engine Failure During Cruise

items.t: ACCOMPLISH ECAM ACTIONS · ATC route clearance when workload permits
items.s: load the new route and MANAGE NAV
items.quote: When ATC clearance is received, load the new route into FMS and MANAGE NAV.
items.ref: PRC p7 Engine Failure During Cruise

items.t: RESET DRIFT DOWN ALTITUDE IN FCU
items.s: REC MAX EO (PROG 1R) · V/S below 500 ft/min: select V/S -500 and A/THR ON
items.quote: When the V/S becomes less than 500 ft/min, select V/S -500 ft/min and A/THR ON.
items.ref: PRC p7 Engine Failure During Cruise

items.t: ADJUST SPEED · ETOPS: 290 kt / M 0.82
items.s: standard strategy 300 kt / M 0.82 · obstacle strategy green dot until clear
items.quote: For ETOPS: set 290 kts/ M 0.82
items.ref: PRC p7 Engine Failure During Cruise

items.t: Contact company · position report every 80 min or 10° · monitor fuel predictions · landing weight and performance
items.s: amended release, landing performance, weather, special assistance · overweight: QRH Overweight Landing
items.quote: Report position every 80 minutes or less / 10º or less, as required by ATC or company.
items.ref: PRC p7 Engine Failure During Cruise

items.t: Diversion speed · approved One-Engine-Inoperative Cruise Speed
items.s: Captain may deviate after assessing the emergency and fuel remaining
items.quote: The Captain has the authority to deviate from this planned speed profile after assessing the emergency and considering fuel remaining.

items.t: Pick the field · least time at or near cruise altitude
items.s: ETPs use planning-time lower-altitude winds · a closer non-ETOPS airport may be better
items.quote: Since the vast majority of diversions are not due to a mechanical issue requiring a descent well below cruise altitude, the Flight Crew should be continuously aware of the airport that would take the least amount of time to fly to at or near cruise altitude.

items.t: Fuel · CP/ETP critical fuel is a dispatch requirement only
items.s: no requirement to divert before the CP if destination fuel is above arrival requirements; Dispatcher adjusts altitude, speed, alternate, routing
items.quote: Arriving at the CP/ETP with Fuel On Board (FOB) equal to or greater than the fuel required by the critical fuel scenario is only a dispatch requirement.

items.t: 1 · Turn to offset from the route
items.s: Special Procedures for In-Flight Contingencies
items.quote: • Turn to offset from the route utilizing the Special Procedures for In-Flight Contingencies.

items.t: 2 · Emergency descent to 10,000 ft or MOCA/Grid MORA, whichever is higher
items.quote: • Perform an Emergency Descent to 10,000 ft or MOCA/Grid MORA, whichever is higher.

items.t: 3 · Below FL290 (or sooner if cleared) proceed directly to the nearest suitable airport
items.quote: • Below FL290, or sooner if cleared by ATC, proceed directly to the nearest suitable airport.

items.t: 4 · When level · Flight Plan one-engine diversion speed, or LRC for a two-engine decompression
items.quote: • When level, use the Flight Plan one-engine diversion speed or (AS) Long Range Cruise (LRC) for two-engine decompression.

items.t: Get a revised clearance first, whenever possible
items.quote: If an aircraft is unable to continue the flight in accordance with its ATC clearance, a revised clearance shall be obtained, whenever possible, prior to initiating any action.

items.t: 1 · Turn at least 30° left or right · parallel same-direction track offset 5 nm
items.quote: Specifically, the pilot shall leave the cleared track or ATS route by initially turning at least 30° to the right or to the left, in order to establish and maintain a parallel, same direction track or ATS route offset 5 nm.

items.t: Choose the turn direction
items.s: position vs the track system · adjacent track flight levels · direction to an alternate · any SLOP · terrain
items.quote: • Aircraft position relative to any organized track or ATS route system • Direction of flights and flight levels allocated on adjacent tracks • Direction to an alternate airport • Any strategic lateral offset being flown • Terrain clearance

items.t: 2 · Below FL290 before diverting (unless cleared) · once on the parallel route, 500 ft vertical offset
items.s: maintain the flight level until 5 nm offset if possible; minimize the rate of descent
items.quote: Once established on a parallel route, establish a 500-ft vertical offset and proceed as required by the situation, or if an ATC clearance has been obtained, proceed in accordance with the clearance.

items.t: 3 · TCAS TA/RA · all exterior lights ON · squawk 7700 when able
items.quote: Turn on all aircraft exterior lights (commensurate with appropriate operating limitations). Keep the transponder on at all times and, when able, squawk 7700, as appropriate.

items.t: 4 · Broadcast on the frequency in use and 121.5 (backup 123.45)
items.s: identification · nature of distress · intentions · position with route or track · flight level · MAYDAY or PAN-PAN three times
items.quote: Establish communications with and alert nearby aircraft by broadcasting on the frequencies in use and at suitable intervals on 121.5 MHz (or, as a backup, on the inter-pilot air-to-air frequency 123.45 MHz): aircraft identification, the nature of the distress condition, intention of the pilot, position (including the ATS route designator or the track code, as appropriate), and flight level.

items.t: ETOPS · engine shutdown or ETOPS-critical failure
items.s: advise ATC as soon as practical, remind of type, request expeditious handling
items.quote: ETOPS – If these contingency procedures are employed as a result of an engine shutdown or failure of an ETOPS-critical system, advise ATC of the situation as soon as practical, remind ATC of the type of aircraft, and request expeditious handling.

items.t: Request first · “WEATHER DEVIATION REQUIRED” or CPDLC lateral downlink
items.s: urgency: “PAN-PAN” three times or CPDLC urgency downlink
items.quote: • Stating “WEATHER DEVIATION REQUIRED” to indicate that priority is desired on the frequency and for ATC response; or • Requesting a weather deviation using a CPDLC lateral downlink message.

items.t: No clearance · Captain exercises emergency authority
items.s: deviate away from the track system · broadcast on the frequency in use and 121.5 / 123.45 · watch TCAS · exterior lights ON
items.quote: • If possible, deviate away from an organized track or route system.

items.t: Less than 5 nm · maintain the assigned flight level
items.quote: • For deviations less than 5 nm, maintain assigned flight level.

items.t: 5 nm or more · level change at about 5 nm from track
items.s: EAST (0° to 179° magnetic): LEFT descend 300 ft, RIGHT climb 300 ft · WEST (180° to 359°): LEFT climb 300 ft, RIGHT descend 300 ft
items.quote: Direction of Flight Deviations ≥5 NM Altitude Change LEFT DESCEND 300 ft EAST (0° to 179° magnetic) RIGHT CLIMB 300 ft LEFT CLIMB 300 ft WEST (180° to 359° magnetic) RIGHT DESCEND 300 ft

items.t: Returning to track · assigned flight level within about 5 nm of centerline
items.s: keep trying for a clearance
items.quote: When returning to track or cleared route, be at its assigned flight level when the aircraft is within approximately 5 nm of the centerline, and if contact was not established prior to deviating, continue to attempt to contact ATC to obtain a clearance.

items.t: 0.0 to 2.0 nm RIGHT of centerline only, 0.1 nm increments
items.s: no ATC clearance required, ATC need not be advised · offset at the oceanic entry, centerline by the oceanic exit
items.quote: SLOP will be applied in relation to a route or track; the aircraft may fly zero, up to a maximum of 2 nm right of course only, from 0.0 - 2.0 nm, right of centerline (in 0.1 nm increments). SLOP left of course is not authorized.

items.t: Overtaking · offset to create the least wake for the aircraft overtaken
items.quote: Any aircraft overtaking another aircraft is to offset within the confines of this procedure, if capable, so as to create the least amount of wake turbulence for the aircraft being overtaken.

items.t: Polygons · IFR High and Low charts in Jeppesen FD Pro
items.s: areas of high terrain where a descent directly to 10,000 ft may not be possible · procedure in the detail drawer (tap the label)
items.quote: Polygons are located in the IFR High and IFR Low charts in Jeppesen FD Pro and denote areas of high terrain where a descent directly to 10,000 ft may not be possible.

items.t: A330 initial descent altitude · always 17,000 ft or FL170
items.quote: (737/A330) Initial descent altitude is always 17,000 ft or FL170.

items.t: Exit Toward Fix · “Exit Twd” + fix
items.s: not necessary to fly to the fix
items.quote: 2. Exit Toward Fix polygons are labeled “Exit Twd” followed by the fix to be flown towards to exit the polygon. It is not necessary to fly to the Exit Towards fix.

items.t: To Fix then Route · fix, then the route
items.s: FD Pro shows the escape route and fixes
items.quote: 3. To Fix then Route polygons are labeled with the fix that should be flown to, and then the route that should be flown subsequently.

items.t: Initial turn distance is built in · do not enter another polygon below its altitude unless terrain clearance is assured
items.quote: Do not enter another polygon while navigating at less than the altitude indicated in the polygon detail drawer unless terrain clearance is assured.

items.t: No Ops Area · never
items.quote: Dispatchers and pilots will not permit flights to proceed through any areas charted as “No Ops Area.”

items.t: The PIC is expected and encouraged to exercise sound judgment when applying these procedures (FOM 11.2.9).
Time of useful consciousness is very limited · quick-don masks within 5 seconds, one hand
