items.t: Aircraft procedure: see Emer Descent (QRH 22.02A).
Captain decides · hand on the thrust levers until V1, PF or PM
items.s: decision and stop action must be made prior to V1
items.quote: It is therefore recommended that the Captain keeps the hand on the thrust levers until the aircraft reaches V1, whether the Captain is Pilot Flying (PF) or Pilot Monitoring (PM).

items.t: Captain: “GO” · malfunction before V1 without rejecting
items.quote: - If a malfunction occurs before V1, for which the Captain does not intend to reject the takeoff, the Captain will announce the intention by calling "GO".

items.t: Captain: “STOP” · confirms the reject and that the Captain has control
items.s: the only hand-over of control without “I have control”
items.quote: - If a decision is made to reject the takeoff, the Captain calls "STOP". This call both confirms the decision to reject the takeoff and also states that the Captain now has control. It is the only time that hand-over of control is not accompanied by the phrase "I have control".

items.t: Below 100 kt · Captain discretion
items.s: seriously consider discontinuing for any ECAM warning/caution
items.quote: The Captain should seriously consider discontinuing the takeoff, if any ECAM warning/caution is activated.

items.t: Above 100 kt and below V1 · go-minded
items.s: 1 fire warning or severe damage · 2 sudden loss of engine thrust · 3 unambiguous indications the aircraft will not fly safely · 4 any ECAM alert
items.quote: 1. Fire warning, or severe damage 2. Sudden loss of engine thrust 3. Malfunctions or conditions that give unambiguous indications that the aircraft will not fly safely 4. Any ECAM alert.

items.t: Not a reject above 100 kt · EGT red line · nose gear vibration · tire failure V1 minus 20 kt to V1
items.s: the V1 call has precedence over any other call
items.quote: Exceeding the EGT red line or nose gear vibration should not result in the decision to reject takeoff above 100 kt.

items.t: Above V1 · takeoff must be continued
items.quote: Takeoff must be continued, because it may not be possible to stop the aircraft on the remaining runway.

items.t: ECAM inhibits non-essential warnings from 80 kt to 1 500 ft (or 2 min after lift-off); any warning in this period is significant (FCTM).
Autobrake MAX decelerating · Captain avoids pressing the pedals
items.s: inoperative autobrake or reject prior to 72 kt: reduce thrust and apply maximum pressure on both pedals, hold to the stop
items.quote: - If the autobrake is inoperative or if the takeoff is rejected prior to 72 kt (autobrake not active and no deployment of spoilers), the captain simultaneously reduces thrust and applies maximum pressure on both pedals.

items.t: Brake response not appropriate · FULL manual braking · IF IN DOUBT, TAKE OVER MANUALLY
items.s: normal braking inoperative: LOSS OF BRAKING memory items
items.quote: - If the brake response does not seem appropriate for the runway condition, FULL manual braking should be applied and maintained. If IN DOUBT, TAKE OVER MANUALLY.

items.t: Full reverse may be used to a complete stop · reduce passing 70 kt if runway permits
items.quote: Full reverse may be used until coming to a complete stop. But, if there is enough runway available at the end of the deceleration, it is preferable to reduce reverse thrust when passing 70 kt.

items.t: PM: “DECEL” · deceleration felt and confirmed by the speed trend
items.s: DECEL light only at 80 % of the selected rate; not proof of autobrake operation
items.quote: - Announcing the deceleration means that the deceleration is felt by the crew, and confirmed by the Vc trend on the PFD.

items.t: Stopped with autobrake MAX · release the brakes before taxi by disarming the spoilers
items.s: do not vacate until it is clear an evacuation is not necessary
items.quote: Do not attempt to vacate the runway, until it is absolutely clear that an evacuation is not necessary and that it is safe to do so.

items.t: Departure Change
After V1 · continue · handling first
items.s: stabilize pitch and airspeed, establish the flight path before the ECAM procedure
items.quote: If an engine fails after V1, the flight crew must continue the takeoff. The essential and primary tasks are associated with the aircraft handling.

items.t: On the ground · rudder conventionally to hold the centerline
items.quote: The flight crew should use the rudder conventionally to maintain the aircraft on the runway centerline.

items.t: At VR · rotate about 3°/s toward 12.5°
items.s: high FLEX temperatures and low VR need precise handling; 12.5° ensures the aircraft becomes airborne
items.quote: At VR, the flight crew should rotate the aircraft using a continuous pitch rate of approximately 3 °/s towards an initial pitch attitude of 12.5 °.

items.t: Safely airborne · follow SRS · center the blue beta target with rudder
items.s: SRS targets the failure speed (V2 to V2+15) · lateral normal law is stable, no rush on the pedals
items.quote: Therefore, laterally, the aircraft is a stable platform and no rush is required to use the rudder pedals.

items.t: PM: “POSITIVE RATE” · PF: “GEAR UP”
items.quote: Gear retraction POSITIVE RATE GEAR UP GEAR UP

items.t: Rudder trim · relieve pedal pressure with the beta target centered · then engage the AP
items.s: AP engaged: rudder trim managed by the AP, release pedal pressure; a maintained pedal deflection may disengage the AP
items.quote: The flight crew should use the rudder trim to gradually relieve the pressure from the rudder pedals while keeping the beta target centered. When the aircraft is properly trimmed, the PF should engage the AP.

items.t: Performance short · confirm gear up · consider TOGA
items.s: derated takeoff: TOGA below F speed can lead to loss of control · takeoff thrust limited to 10 min
items.quote: If the takeoff is performed at derated takeoff thrust, selecting TOGA at a speed below F can lead to loss of control of the aircraft.

items.t: Trajectory first · delay acceleration only to secure the engine
items.s: ENG MASTER OFF (no damage) · AGENT 1 DISCH (damage) · fire out or AGENT 2 DISCH (fire)
items.quote: "Secure the engine" means that the flight crew should continue the ECAM procedure until: - "ENG MASTER OFF" in the case of an engine failure without damage, or - "AGENT 1 DISCH" in the case of an engine failure with damage, or - Fire extinguished or "AGENT 2 DISCH" in the case of an engine fire.

items.t: EO acceleration altitude · ALT pb or push V/S to level off · flaps on schedule

items.quote: At the engine-out (EO) acceleration altitude, the flight crew should press the ALT pb or push the V/S knob to level off and to enable the speed to increase.

items.t: Speed trend at green dot · pull ALT for OP CLB · THRUST LEVERS MCT when LVR MCT flashes
items.s: already in FLX/MCT: CL then back to MCT
items.quote: When the speed trend arrow reaches the green dot speed, pull the ALT knob to engage OP CLB. Set the thrust levers to MCT when the LVR MCT message flashes on the FMA (this message appears, when the speed index reaches green dot).

items.t: Established on the final takeoff path · continue ECAM to the STATUS page
items.s: ensure the Acceleration flow · consider relight if no damage · review STATUS
items.quote: When the aircraft is established on the final takeoff flight path, the flight crew should continue the ECAM procedure until the STATUS page appears.

items.t: One engine out flight path · per the departure briefing
items.s: EOSID · SID · radar vector
items.quote: The flight crew flies the one engine-out flight path in accordance with the departure briefing performed at the gate: - The EOSID, or - The SID, or - Radar vector, etc.

items.s: FMGS predictions switch to engine-out; pre-selected speeds deleted
items.quote: If the failure occurs above V2 however, maintain the SRS commanded attitude. In any case, the minimum speed must be V2.
